layout.heading: What Is Measurement Preventative Maintenance *& How It Works*
body: Measurement Preventative Services in UAE are scheduled inspection, calibration, and software maintenance activities performed on measurement and metering equipment before a fault causes lost revenue or a compliance breach. Unlike reactive repair, this scheduled maintenance oil and gas instrumentation approach catches drift, wear, and outdated firmware while the system is still within tolerance, avoiding the unplanned shutdowns that come with equipment failure discovered too late. At General Tech Automation, our team manages an instrumentation reliability program covering truck loading system maintenance, rail loading system maintenance, satellite well testing system maintenance, and flow measurement system maintenance. Each visit includes measurement system audit and inspection against manufacturer tolerances and site-specific accuracy requirements, so custody transfer accuracy verification is documented at every interval, not assumed between visits.

items.title: Gas Analyzer Maintenance and Calibration
items.description: Our gas analyzer calibration services cover process and emissions-monitoring analyzers, verifying accuracy against certified reference gases and correcting drift before it triggers a compliance flag. Process gas analyzer support includes sensor replacement, filter changes, and software checks, keeping analyzers within regulatory emissions compliance metering tolerances between full recalibration cycles, typically every 3 to 6 months depending on service duty.

items.title: Custody Transfer Metering Maintenance
items.description: Custody transfer metering maintenance protects the accuracy that both buyer and seller rely on for billing, since even small metering drift translates directly into lost or disputed revenue. Our metering skid calibration and measurement system calibration UAE service verifies flow computers, provers, and transmitters against traceable standards, with results documented for audit and regulatory review.

items.title: Net Oil Computer and Wellhead Systems

Skid mounted metering maintenance at remote wellsites is scheduled around production windows to avoid unnecessary well downtime.

items.q: How often should metering systems be calibrated?
a: Most custody transfer and gas analyzer systems are calibrated every 3 to 6 months, though the exact interval depends on manufacturer recommendation, regulatory requirement, and how critical the measurement point is to billing or compliance. High-value custody transfer points are often calibrated more frequently than general process monitoring instruments.

items.q: What does a preventative maintenance contract for instrumentation include?
a: A preventative maintenance contract instrumentation agreement typically includes scheduled inspection, calibration against traceable standards, software and firmware updates, and documented reporting for every visit. Contracts can be scoped to cover a single analyzer or an entire site's measurement and metering infrastructure under one fixed schedule.

items.q: Why is custody transfer accuracy verification important?
a: Custody transfer accuracy verification confirms that a meter is reading within agreed tolerance for billing purposes between two parties, such as a buyer and seller of oil or gas. Even small drift can translate into significant financial disputes over time, so regular verification protects both parties and supports regulatory compliance.

items.q: How quickly can a technician respond to a measurement system failure?
a: For contracted clients, emergency measurement failures affecting custody transfer or compliance readings are typically prioritised, with technicians dispatched within 4 to 8 hours across Dubai, Sharjah, Abu Dhabi, and Fujairah. Non-critical issues are scheduled into the next available preventative maintenance visit, and clients on a fixed contract typically receive priority slotting ahead of ad-hoc callers.
